issues.legal_issue: Damages under an indemnity for a sale of voidable title are limited to loss actually sustained when the purchaser remains in possession.
material_facts: A seller conveyed property that included his minor son's share and gave an indemnity against loss if the sale of that share was later set aside.
After attaining majority, the son obtained a decree setting aside the sale of his share, but the purchasers remained in possession.
A relative of the purchasers bought the share at a court sale on their behalf, and the purchasers paid the court-sale price and incurred expenses defending the suit that challenged the sale.
The High Court limited damages to those actual expenditures, rather than awarding half the original consideration, and the Supreme Court upheld that limitation.
issues.conclusion: The purchasers were entitled to recover only their actual loss, including the court-sale price and the expenses incurred defending the challenge to the sale; they could not recover half the original consideration while they remained in possession.
issues.legal_principle: Where a sale conveys a title that is voidable rather than void from the outset, setting the sale aside does not by itself establish a breach causing loss under an indemnity or warranty of title. While the purchaser remains in possession, loss of the property has not occurred; damages are recoverable only for loss actually sustained. The Court approved Subbaroya Reddiar v. Rajagopala Reddiar (1915) ILR 38 Mad. 887, Muhammad Siddiq v. Muhammad Nuh, ILR 52 All. 604, and Gulabchand Daulatram v. Suryaji Rao Ganpatrao, AIR 1950 Bom. 401. Subbaroya Reddiar also referred to Hanuman Kamat v. Hanuman Mandur, ILR 19 Cal. 123 (PC), and Bassu Kuar v. Dhum Singh, ILR 11 All. 47 (PC).

rule.if: indemnity_claim_after_voidable_sale and purchaser_kept_possession and purchaser_paid_to_reacquire_share and purchaser_incurred_defence_costs

predicates.indemnity_claim_after_voidable_sale: A purchaser or successor sought recovery under an indemnity arising from a sale of property that could be avoided by another person.
predicates.purchaser_kept_possession: The purchaser or successor continued to possess the disputed property after the sale was set aside.
predicates.purchaser_paid_to_reacquire_share: The purchaser or someone acting on the purchaser's behalf paid to acquire the disputed share at a court sale.
predicates.purchaser_incurred_defence_costs: The purchaser incurred expenses defending proceedings that challenged the sale or the purchaser's possession.

issues.definition: When an indemnity claim follows an avoidable sale and the purchaser retains possession but incurs expenses to reacquire the share and defend the challenge, the recoverable damages are limited to actual loss.
